known_limitations: Global /mcp/ endpoint: v1.1.1 refuses team-scoped member tokens with 'Streamable HTTP RBAC denied: permission=tools.execute' while /rpc allows the same call. Fail closed, but agents must use /rpc or /servers/{id}/mcp. Not investigated further (M5).
Criterion 5 is a live upgrade rehearsal (v1.1.0 -> v1.1.1); MC-05 as an automated test is stage C.
Arguments and non-identity _meta keys from the agent reach the connector unchanged; the connector must read identity only from the verified JWS (SEC-01).
target-platform-v1.md has one more VERIFY (tool_pre_invoke cannot pause for a human) outside AC-M4-04; not changed.
ContextForge docs (identity-propagation.md) claim the HMAC covers canonical JSON of all claims and adds claims_signature to _meta; the v1.1.1 code does neither. Worth reporting upstream; not done.

The agent's own headers (X-Tenant-Id, X-GxG-Identity, ...) do not reach the connector on the v1.1.1 MCP path even with passthrough allowlisted (critic, cycle 1). The 'plugin overwrites a forged X-GxG-Identity' claim was removed; the signature is the guard. The passthrough-misconfig stage was removed.

Variant C is a prototype: key from a file (chmod 644 on the stand for the image's non-root user), tenant/connector maps in YAML, in-process jti set in the verifier. SEC-03 requires a jti store shared by all connector replicas until exp + skew (M1).

The adapter runs inside the ContextForge process: code execution in ContextForge gives the signing key and lets an attacker mint a JWS for any tenant (built-in A is no better). Production: secret store, short kid rotation, alert on unknown kid.

principal = local part of the ContextForge user email (the plugin sees email, not the user UUID). Recreating an agent with the same email gives the same principal and its grants; agent emails must never be reused (registry tombstone). Written in the ADR.
Paths without tool_pre_invoke were read in code, not run: direct_proxy gateways (off by default, set false explicitly), resources/read and prompts/get (arrive without identity, connector refuses).
Canonical JSON is Python json.dumps(sort_keys, compact separators, ensure_ascii=False), not RFC 8785; floats serialize differently from JCS. Both sides must use the same function (SEC-03).
Commit 8bb6efe (re-apply SEC-02/SEC-03) also carries the deletion of compose.passthrough-misconfig.yaml and its two evidence files, staged earlier; history not rewritten.

ToolPreInvokePayload.headers is deprecated in cpex 0.1.4 (use extensions.http.headers); v1.1.1 tool_service applies only modified_payload.headers to the upstream request, so migration is not possible yet. When the field is removed, identity stops reaching connectors (fail closed, outage). ADR criterion 5 and 'Что дальше': MC-05 must assert X-GxG-Identity arrives and is accepted; plugin migrates to modified_extensions with write_headers once ContextForge applies it.
Echo records the verdict but still answers a rejected call with the echo result; refusing with an error is the M5 connector's job.
